title: Finite scalar square for the two normalized classical fibres
statement: For the normalized comparison data of [def-zl-classical-two-fibre-data] and the normalized finite scalar PBC fibre maps of [def-per-adic-fibre-comparison-data], finite scalar compatibility is the commuting square between the canonical sf point scalar map and the normalized PBC scalar map, conjugated by the two fibre comparisons. Require the square for every finite inclusion E into L, including identity, every lisse object and its scalar-extended model, and every geometric point. The actual comparison under J is characterized by its image under the faithful continuous derived realization: it is the composite of the normalized sf derived scalar map of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] and the normalized PBC derived scalar map of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], conjugated by the sf/PBC realization comparison. Retain the equality of their normalized coefficient maps and the equality between the zero and characteristic-parameter presentations of scalar extension from [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Use the actual finite coefficient point and tensor/cohomology scalar maps of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and [lem-weil-cohomology-commutes-scalar-extension]. No arbitrary scalar comparison replaces a canonical construction.
